solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Toy castle setter's sweetheart's found in stall

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
a castle is a fortified stronghold, a fort
the setter's = the setter is, written I'M from the setter's own mouth
the sweet heart: the central letter of the word sweet

explanation.surface: A child's toy fort, built by the setter's beloved, turns up on a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is not a lover but the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter. 'setter's' means the setter is, so I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay deliberately so as to gain time, the idiom meant by the phrase.

clue.text: Twist lid off organ

indicators.note: off means the lid is taken away from the name

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan, so Twist calls up his first name
a lid is a round cover, pictured as the letter O

explanation.surface: A grisly instruction: twist the lid off a jar holding an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like a verb but is the surname of Dickens's Oliver; take off its round 'lid' O.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is a large internal organ that processes blood and makes bile.

clue.text: Rather tipsy-sounding, joins central private seminary

indicators.note: said the way a drunk slurs it, so the s becomes sh

parts.note: 'Rather!' is an emphatic old-fashioned yes

indicators.note: central means only the middle of the word private is kept, its outer letters dropped

explanation.surface: Someone a little drunk agrees noisily before enrolling at a private seminary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy-sounding' turns YES into a slurred YESH; 'central' keeps the middle IVA of 'private', shedding PR and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeshiva is an Orthodox Jewish college for studying the Talmud, a religious seminary.

clue.text: Alternative point fabricated by Opposition leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition
fabricated means made up, so the letters of point are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: A political charge: the Opposition leader has invented an alternative argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' looks like an accusation of lying, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of the choices open to you, another possibility or alternative.

clue.text: Rent a bar to uplift Escamillo, maybe

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, meaning tore

indicators.note: in a down entry, uplifting a word reads it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bar of metal is a rod

explanation.surface: Tear a bar loose so as to raise up Escamillo, perhaps on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to uplift' turns ROD into DOR. Escamillo is the bullfighter in Bizet's opera Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo is the famous fictional bullfighter in Carmen, an example of the type.

clue.text: Be careful about class approach…

parts.note: to mind something is to be careful about it, as in mind the step
a set is a group or class, as in a school teaching set

explanation.surface: A teacher's warning to take care how one handles the class, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a habitual way of thinking, one's mental approach or attitude.

clue.text: …to sectarian PR circulating; 1

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so these letters go round into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a careful approach to sectarian propaganda that is doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 1 across, PLAY FOR TIME; the ellipsis ties the surface to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to put things off and delay, which is stalling for time.

clue.text: Expert first violin is leader of orchestra — about to turn out right?

indicators.note: first says the violin letter comes at the very front of the answer

parts.note: V is an abbreviation for violin, as in a score's part marked V

indicators.note: about means going around, so the is-plus-orchestra pair wraps the next part
to turn means the following words are flipped back to front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of orchestra

explanation.surface: Is the first violin, who leads the orchestra, about to prove right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses the pair out-and-right, which 'about' places inside ISO. In Britain the orchestra's leader really is the first violin, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding technical skill, a master or expert.

clue.text: Ferret out nice materials for fraudster

indicators.note: materials are raw stuff to be worked into something new, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Investigators sniff out fine fabrics to catch a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferret out' looks like the phrasal verb but all three words are anagram fodder, signalled by 'materials'.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeiter makes fake money or goods, a kind of forger and fraudster.

clue.text: Parties wither after U-turn about start of voting

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word goes round the next letter
a U-turn sends the word back the way it came

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or dry up, so wither

indicators.note: the start of voting is its first letter

explanation.surface: Political parties lose heart after a policy reversal at the start of voting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after U-turn' turns SEAR into RAES; 'about' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raves are large all-night dance parties, typically with electronic music.

clue.text: Millionaire star losing rag initially with trendy Oscar director

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Chris Tarrant was the host of the UK quiz show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of rag

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rich celebrity, keeping his temper at first, wins an Oscar with a fashionable director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing rag initially' drops an R from TARRANT. 'Oscar' looks like the film award but is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is a famous American film director, an example of the type.

clue.text: Bears perchance with vicar on a river trip

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Maybe bears join the vicar on a boat trip down the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as an outing, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnivora is the order of meat-eating mammals, which includes bears, cats and dogs.

clue.text: Resolute about Anya?

definitions.meaning: determined on doing something, firmly intent
Anya ... was an American historical novelist, author of Katherine

explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something means resolutely determined about it; Anya is the novelist's first name.

clue.text: Brutal dictator back in Albania

indicators.note: in means the reversed name sits inside the code

parts.note: AL is the international code for Albania

indicators.note: back means the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: A cruel tyrant returns to Albania.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin ruled Uganda in the 1970s; AL is Albania's international vehicle code. 'back' reverses him and 'in' places him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, animal means physical and bestial, so savage or brutal.

clue.text: 'One's royalty!', we hear (from Charles perhaps — performing impressions?)

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: 'One's royalty' is what a royal saying one is would mean: I'm prince

explanation.surface: Charles, putting on a show of royal grandeur, announces his own status.
explanation.walkthrough: Royals traditionally say 'one' for I, so Charles would say 'I'm prince'; spoken quickly it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprints are marks pressed into a surface, that is impressions.

clue.text: After quiet over, new English opener is to 1

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the opener of English is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: after a quiet over, a new English opening batsman comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 1 across, PLAY FOR TIME. 'opener' reads as a batsman but takes E.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to put something off to a later date, a way of stalling.

clue.text: Fit permit into a deficient compact

indicators.note: into means one word goes inside the other
deficient means lacking, here losing its last letter

parts.note: thick means dense, closely packed or compact
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Squeezing a permit into an inadequate agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compact' looks like an agreement but means dense; 'deficient' drops its last letter and 'into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes someone strong, fit and in good physical shape.

clue.text: Ulster Society's exhibiting painters' work

parts.note: an ulster is a long, loose belted overcoat, a kind of topcoat
S is an abbreviation for Society

explanation.surface: A Northern Ireland art society is showing paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like the province but is the overcoat named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Top coats are the final layers of paint that decorators apply, so a painter's work.

clue.text: Dip in wading pool cancelled sadly — a self-inflicted loss

indicators.note: cancelled means the word Dip is struck out of the letters
sadly means things go wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A swim in the paddling pool is called off, a disappointing setback.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D, I and P out of WADING POOL and rearrange the rest, WANGOOL, as directed by 'cancelled' and 'sadly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring into your own net in football is the classic self-inflicted setback, used of any self-harming error.

clue.text: 1 by stripping Lilliput of food

indicators.note: stripping means peeling away the outer letters to reveal the run inside

explanation.surface: Stripping Lilliput of its food would be one way to delay the little people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 1 across, PLAY FOR TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off is to postpone or delay, which is what stalling does.

clue.text: Yankee having difficulties raised in 24 or 28?

definitions.meaning: in American slang, someone in a fix or cornered is in this state
lifted into a leylandii or a black cherry, both trees

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is American slang for being stuck or in trouble, and literally means perched in branches.

clue.text: Cryptic from Jeremy's ticklish

indicators.note: from means the answer comes out of the run of letters in the following words

explanation.surface: Jeremy's ticklishness is an enigma.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic means having a hidden, secret or obscure meaning, which is what cryptic means.

clue.text: Look in notes for links?

indicators.note: in means the look goes inside the notes

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give NN
an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A puzzle: check your notes to find the cufflinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Nairn is a Scottish town on the Moray Firth famous for its golf links; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn has a celebrated seaside golf course, so the town stands for links by example.

clue.text: Neighbours may regard them as alien — idly let go

indicators.note: let go means released from order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Neighbours may resent things as foreign when they are carelessly allowed to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the trees: fast-growing conifer hedges notoriously cause neighbour disputes in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Leyland cypress hedges grow so fast and tall that they are a notorious cause of rows between neighbours.

clue.text: Refused to go up without us, so 1

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upwards
without means the letters of us are taken out of the word

explanation.surface: Someone refused to climb without the rest of us, and so delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' and 'to go up' work in that order: remove first, then read upwards. The definition is 1 across, PLAY FOR TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to put something off until later, a way of stalling for time.

clue.text: Payback time — gift of poor Stuart's oddly mislaid

indicators.note: oddly mislaid means the odd-numbered letters are lost, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Time for revenge: the gift poor Stuart left somewhere has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly mislaid' drops letters 1, 3, 5 and so on of 'gift of poor Stuart', leaving ITFORTAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means retaliation in kind, giving back blow for blow, which is payback.

clue.text: Level firearm partly rearwards — this one?

definitions.text: Level firearm partly rearwards — this one?

indicators.note: rearwards means the piece is read from back to front
partly means only a piece of the words is used

explanation.surface: Aim a gun level, part of it pointing backwards: what sort of gun is it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes ELFIR from 'Level firearm' and 'rearwards' turns it round. The whole clue then points at the very gun involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm that is levelled at a target.

clue.text: Opening bowler to need new ball — it can bear fruit

indicators.note: the opening of bowler is its first letter

parts.note: to lack something is to need it
in cricket slang a new, shiny red ball is a cherry

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the opening bowler needs a new ball, which may bring results.
explanation.walkthrough: A brand-new cricket ball is called a 'cherry' for its bright red shine.
explanation.definitionFit: The black cherry is a tree that produces dark fruit, so it is something that bears fruit.
